patients.summary: Retired construction foreman with long-standing type 2 diabetes, hypertension and chronic atrial fibrillation on warfarin who joins in 2020. Over six years he has diabetic polyneuropathy, a nasal basal cell carcinoma, a pharyngoesophageal diverticulum, endophthalmitis after cataract surgery, a venous air embolism at angiography, a diabetic foot osteomyelitis, an appendiceal abscess and finally a locally advanced mucin-producing pancreatic adenocarcinoma with chronic DIC.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
66 y/o retired construction foreman transferring care from his former primary care office.

HPI: Type 2 diabetes since about 2006, on metformin the whole time, no hypoglycemia. Hypertension about as long, on lisinopril and HCTZ. Atrial fibrillation picked up at his old practice around 2016; has been on warfarin since, INR drawn monthly there. No palpitations he notices, no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no bleeding.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, chronic atrial fibrillation.
PSH: tonsils and adenoids out at age 7.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, HCTZ 12.5 mg daily, warfarin 5 mg daily (adjusted to INR), atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: father had type 2 diabetes and an MI at 72. Mother hypertension and a basal cell skin cancer. An uncle on his father's side had pancreatic cancer.
Social: smoked about a pack a day for 20 years, stopped in 2016. A drink or two a week, socially. Retired foreman, ran residential framing crews for decades.

Exam: well-appearing, comfortable. Vitals as charted. Heart irregularly irregular, rate controlled, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Feet: skin intact, pulses present, monofilament sensation intact today.

A/P:
1. Type 2 diabetes - A1c sent. Continue metformin.
2. Hypertension - at goal, continue lisinopril/HCTZ. BMP today.
3. Chronic AF on warfarin - CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (age, HTN, DM). We will manage INR here; RN to set him up with monthly checks, goal 2-3. INR today.
4. Lipids - on atorvastatin 40, lipid panel today.
5. Health maintenance - will request old records including colonoscopy. Flu shot and Tdap at a nurse visit next month.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt with results. INR 2.4, in range: continue warfarin 5 mg daily, next INR in about 6 weeks with the nurse visit. A1c 7.8, kidney function normal, LDL 74. PCP reviewed. Pt verbalized understanding.

documents.title: Former primary care records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records received by fax from the patient's prior primary care office, 48 pages, scanned.

Summary for chart (PCP):
- Problem list: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, atrial fibrillation (noted 2016, started on warfarin then).
- Colonoscopy 2017: normal to the cecum, no polyps; advised repeat at 10 years.
- INR log 2019-2020: mostly 2.0-2.8 on 5 mg daily.
- Med list matches what he brought.
- No drug allergies recorded.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for high-dose flu and Tdap (last tetanus shot he can remember was in his forties, not in old records). Both given L deltoid / R deltoid, tolerated well. INR drawn: 2.6. No bleeding or bruising, no missed doses, no new meds or antibiotics. Continue warfarin 5 mg daily. Next INR in 4 weeks.

documents.title: Anticoagulation
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR 2.2. Spoke with pt - no changes in diet, no bleeding. Continue 5 mg daily. Recheck 4 wks.

documents.title: Anticoagulation

documents.body: INR 3.1, slightly above goal. Pt says Thanksgiving week he ate less greens than usual, otherwise nothing new. No bleeding. Take 2.5 mg (half tab) tonight only, then back to 5 mg daily. Recheck 2 weeks with his visit.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing fine. Taking meds as prescribed. Home sugars in the 140s-170s fasting. No lows. No chest pain or palpitations, no bleeding on warfarin.

O: Vitals as charted. Irregularly irregular, rate in the 70s. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
- T2DM: A1c 7.9 today, about where it was in September. Continue metformin 1000 BID.
- HTN: at goal on lisinopril 10 / HCTZ 12.5.
- AF on warfarin: INR 2.5 today, back in range after last month's 3.1. Continue 5 mg daily.
- COVID vaccine: encouraged when his age group opens up; he plans to go to a pharmacy.

RTC 3 months.

events.reason: Diabetes follow-up; feet burning at night

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine diabetes check. Both COVID shots done. Mentions at the end that his feet have been burning at night for the last few months, both sides, sometimes pins and needles; says it is worse when he gets into bed. No injuries, no sores he has seen. Hasn't changed shoes.

O: Vitals as charted. Heart irregular, rate controlled. Feet look fine - no calluses or breaks in the skin. Didn't have time for a full sensory exam today.

A/P:
- T2DM, A1c 8.0 today. Continue metformin.
- Burning feet, likely diabetes related but will check B12 (on metformin for years) and TSH first. Book a dedicated visit to look at the feet properly.
- HTN controlled. BMP today.
- AF: INR checks continue with RN.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Eugene - your B12 (410) and thyroid test (TSH 1.9) are both normal, and your kidney numbers and potassium are fine. A1c is 8.0. We'll go over the feet in detail at the visit you booked. Have a good weekend.

documents.title: Anticoagulation
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR 2.1. Continue 5 mg daily. Reminder card mailed for next month.

documents.title: Anticoagulation
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Missed last week's draw - says he was helping a friend frame a shed and forgot. INR today 2.4. Continue 5 mg daily.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic polyneuropathy

medications.sig: Apply a thin layer to both feet twice daily; wash hands after use

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - feet
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here about his feet as planned. About six months now of burning and tingling in both feet. Worst at night, keeps him up some nights. No falls or injuries, no fevers, no swelling. B12 and TSH were normal in March.

O: Vitals as charted.
Feet: skin intact, no ulcers, no color change. Vibration sense reduced at both great toes and ankles; pinprick dulled to just above the ankles both sides, stocking pattern. Strength 5/5 at hips, knees, ankles and toes. Ankle jerks diminished bilaterally, knees 2+.
A1c 8.1.

A/P:
1. Diabetic polyneuropathy, symmetric, sensory. Talked about foot care, checking feet daily, well-fitting shoes. Prefers to avoid another pill. Capsaicin 0.075% cream to both feet twice daily; warned it burns for the first week or two and to wash hands well. Message me in a month with how it's going.
2. T2DM: A1c 8.1. Continue metformin.
3. AF: INR 2.6, continue warfarin per RN.

documents.title: Foot cream
documents.author: patient
documents.body: You asked me to write in about the cream. First week it stung pretty good but I kept at it morning and night like you said. It has been about 4 weeks and the burning is a lot less, sleeping better most nights. Should I keep using it?

documents.title: RE: Foot cream
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it. Yes, keep using it twice a day - it works best with steady use. Let me know if it stops helping.

documents.title: Anticoagulation
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR 1.9, just under. Garden is in, eating a lot of salads and green beans. No missed doses. Take 7.5 mg (1.5 tabs) tonight, then 5 mg daily; try to keep the greens steady rather than up and down. Recheck 2-3 wks or at the physical.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Medicare AWV, first one with us.

Interval: capsaicin cream still helping the feet, uses it most days. Nothing else new. Lives in his own house in town, independent in all ADLs and IADLs, still drives. No falls. Hearing and vision ok with readers. PHQ-2 0. Advance directive: has not done one, information given.

Meds reviewed: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5, warfarin 5 (per INR), atorvastatin 40, capsaicin cream.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Irregularly irregular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no pulsatile mass. Feet: intact skin, reduced vibration at toes unchanged, pulses palpable.

Prevention:
- Colonoscopy 2017 normal per old records, next 2027.
- Lung cancer screening: 20 pack-years, quit 2016 - eligible. Discussed benefits and false positives; he wants it. LDCT ordered.
- AAA screening: ever-smoker man 65-75, ultrasound ordered.
- Hep C and HIV one-time screening today.
- Vaccines: high-dose flu, PCV20, Shingrix #1 today. Shingrix #2 in 2-6 months. COVID booster when eligible.
- Labs: A1c, CMP, CBC, lipids, urine microalbumin.

RTC 3-4 months for diabetes.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your labs from the wellness visit look good. A1c 7.9. Kidney and liver tests normal, urine protein normal, blood count normal, LDL cholesterol in a good range on the atorvastatin. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. INR 2.5. The ultrasound and lung scan schedulers will call you.

reports.text:
INDICATION: AAA screening, 67-year-old male former smoker.
TECHNIQUE: Grayscale and color imaging of the abdominal aorta.
FINDINGS: The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber throughout, maximum diameter 2.1 cm at the infrarenal level. No aneurysm. Iliac arteries normal at their origins. Incidental views of the kidneys show normal size without hydronephrosis.

documents.title: Result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Notified pt aorta ultrasound normal, no aneurysm. No further screening needed per PCP.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Bump on the side of his nose for about a year, slowly bigger. Catches it shaving and it bleeds, then scabs. Doesn't hurt. Mother had a skin cancer removed.

O: Vitals as charted. Small raised lesion on the lateral nose, shiny surface with a few fine vessels. No other lesions on face.

A/P: Nasal lesion - concerning for a basal cell; dermatology referral for evaluation and biopsy. INR 2.3 today, in range.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
INDICATION: Lung cancer screening, baseline. Former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2016.
TECHNIQUE: Low-dose noncontrast CT of the chest.
FINDINGS: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Airways clear. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung screening
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your lung screening CT was negative - no nodules. We'll repeat it each year.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Shingrix #2 given L deltoid, series complete. First dose gave him a sore arm and he felt tired for a day. INR 2.8, continue 5 mg daily. Dermatology appt next week - reminded him to tell them he's on warfarin.

documents.title: Dermatology consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group
Date of service: 12/13/2021
Re: Eugene Connolly, DOB 09/09/1954

Thank you for referring Mr. Connolly, a 67-year-old with diabetes, for a nasal lesion. He reports a bump on the nose for about a year that bleeds now and then when he shaves and is otherwise without symptoms.

Medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, warfarin, atorvastatin, capsaicin cream. Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Exam: On the lateral aspect of the nose there is a 1.5 cm pearly, flesh-colored nodule with overlying telangiectasias and a central depression. No cervical, preauricular or submandibular lymphadenopathy. Remainder of the face, scalp, neck, arms and trunk examined without other suspicious lesions.

Procedure: After consent and local anesthesia, a shave biopsy was taken. Hemostasis with aluminum chloride. Warfarin continued.

Impression: clinically a basal cell carcinoma; pathology pending. Given the location, margin-controlled excision would be recommended if confirmed. We will call him with results.

conditions.label: Basal cell carcinoma of skin of nose

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Skin, lateral nose, shave biopsy.
MICROSCOPIC: Nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and retraction artifact arising from the epidermis and extending into the dermis.
DIAGNOSIS: Basal cell carcinoma, nodular type. Tumor extends to the deep and peripheral margins of the specimen.
reports.conclusion: Basal cell carcinoma, nodular type, lateral nose.

documents.title: Dermatopathology
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Biopsy result from dermatology received and scanned. Nodular basal cell carcinoma, nose. Dermatology scheduling the excision. PCP reviewed, added to problem list.
